messages:
tara: Quick heads-up — noticed a recurring tail-latency spike when running INT8 KV on short prefill sequences (~8 tokens) on A100-80GB. Median looks fine but p95 jumps.
kevin: curious, numbers?
tara: baseline fp16-kv: median 3.4ms / p95 11.8ms. int8-kv: median 3.6ms / p95 48–62ms depending on batch. fp8-kv: median 3.5ms / p95 ~16ms.
maria: that's a big delta. Did you pin to the same kernel/runtime? could be allocator/alignment interaction with the KV buffer.
tara: yes same binary + kernels. suspect fragmentation in KV allocator — saw `nvidia-smi` resident vs allocated oscillations during cold prefill. logs show many small cudaMallocs during prefill stage.
kevin: can you paste the bench output you used?
tara: ```
# bench-prefill --model xlm-13b --quant int8 --kv-mode pref
median_ms: 3.62
p95_ms: 57.9
kv_mem_mb: 1240
gpu_mem_mb: 37856
malloc_calls: 384
```
kevin: malloc_calls=384 for tiny prefill is suspicious. sounds like per-kv-chunk allocs. maybe our roundup to 4k/64k pages causes fragmentation and extra work.
maria: also check allocator trace lines `RT_KV_ALLOC`: they include align sizes and chunk ids. If alignment increased for int8 path (maybe to 512B), that could bloat the working set.
perf-bot: perf-alert: int8-kv p95 regression > 3x on short-prefill vs fp16 — ticket created ML-3458
tara: filed ML-3458 and attached perf traces + nvprof stacks. @kevin can you try a temporary coalesce patch to reduce cudaMalloc frequency? even batched allocs would help isolate.
kevin: on it. I'll implement a micro-coalesce in the KV allocator, run microbake with `--kv-chunk=1m` + `--prefill-batch=8`, and compare.
tara: thanks — I'll also run the same matrix on H100 to see if this is allocator/driver-specific.
maria: note for rollout: int8 saves ~28% KV memory for long contexts, but cold p95 spikes break streaming SLAs. we should gate int8 KV on prefill-length profile until root cause fixed.
kevin: agreed. quick action: reproduce -> patch -> retest A100/H100 -> update canary routing to prefer fp8/fp16 for short-prefill traffic.
tara: :thumbsup:
